# Sea

> Sea is a small programming language with Lua's syntax and Go's runtime model
> (goroutines, channels, select, defer, panic/recover, errors as values),
> implemented as a register-based VM in C with an optional JIT. Sea is not in
> language models' training data: read docs/sea-for-ai.md before writing Sea code.

Key differences from Lua: arrays are 0-indexed and built with `[]` and `a[] = v`;
`len(x)` instead of `#x`; `for k, v in t do` instead of pairs/ipairs; one statement
per line; `{x = 1}` is a sealed struct; maps are `[=]`; errors are values
(`error("msg")`, `is_error(v)`, postfix `?`); no pcall, metatables or Lua patterns.
Check code with `sea check file.sea` (or `sea check -` on stdin, `-f json`), format it with
`sea fmt file.sea`, look up a built-in with `sea doc string.split`. Errors name the failing value and
say what Sea has instead of `table.sort`, `pcall`, `string.gsub`, `#x`, `?:`.

## Docs

- [Sea for AI assistants](docs/sea-for-ai.md): the rules models get wrong, the syntax, verified examples, the standard library and translation tables, in one file
- [Language reference](docs/reference.md): syntax, operators, built-ins, standard library, command line tools
- [External libraries](docs/libs.md): json, yaml, toml, csv, xml, http, ssl, websocket, jwt, sqlite, duckdb, flags, log, test, template, tensor, console, compress (gzip, zip, tar)
- [A tour of Sea](docs/tour.md): example-driven introduction

## Examples

- [examples/](examples/): runnable programs (each directory has a `.sea` file)
- [examples/users](examples/users/): an application on SQLite with a `sea test` suite

## Optional

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): compiler, VM, values, scheduler
- [Memory model](docs/memory.md): reference counting, ownership, cycle collector
